result.summary:
Independently re-derived from docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md itself (not from CODE-DESIGNER's step-01 result.summary) against issue #29's ten ACs, decisions/0007 (binding, read in full), security-invariants.md S9/S10, and the live apps/bot/src source it claims to extend/reuse. One check fails the gate outright (Step 1b check 2d, zero implementation code); every other check was independently verified and found sound, recorded below so rework does not need to re-litigate them.

FAILING CHECK -- 2d, implementation code present. Sec5.1 point 4 and Sec5.2 point 4 write literal, executable TypeScript expressions, not prose/table-stated composition rules: `text = [catalog.reminder24h.prompt, event.title, formatDateTimeInTimezone(...)].join("\n")` and `buttons = [{ label: ..., callbackData: \`reminder24h:confirm:${registrationId}\` }, ...]` in Sec5.1; the caption line-building using inline template-literal expressions (`` `${catalog.reminder3h.doorsLabel} ${formatDateTimeInTimezone(...)}` ``) in Sec5.2 point 4. These are array literals composed with an actual `.join("\n")` method call and template-literal string interpolation -- executable content-assembly code, not a signature ending in `;` and not a prose/table rule statement. This is exactly the pattern this role's own file (.claude/agents/code-designer.md) singles out as having already FAILed the gate twice ('a real one-line predicate... because it's obvious anyway'), and it is a real regression from this project's own established convention for this exact kind of content-shape description: REQ-017.md Sec3.2 describes its structurally identical agendaLines/dateTimeText composition entirely in prose ('rendered as a range... start and end formatted separately, joined with an en dash -- a plain string composition') and a field-to-source table, never as a literal `.join(...)` expression; REQ-025.md Sec4 describes its composeMessage content as prose with an ellipsis ('...build the exact same [...] text as REQ-023 Sec6.3 already does') referencing pre-existing unchanged logic, never new literal array/join/template code. REQ-026.md's Sec5.1/5.2 blocks are new composition logic (this reminder's own text/caption, not a citation to already-existing code), written as runnable TypeScript. Rework: restate Sec5.1 point 4 and Sec5.2 point 4 as a prose ordered-lines table (line 1 = X, line 2 = Y, joined with newline in this order), the same style REQ-017 Sec3.2/Sec4 (row format) and this document's own Sec5.2 closing AC8 paragraph already use elsewhere -- content and field sourcing may stay exactly as specified, only the literal `.join`/array-literal/template-literal syntax must be removed.

EVERYTHING ELSE CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND (re-verify is still required on the reworked doc, but these do not need re-litigating from scratch):

1. AGENDA-SHAPE / DOORS-IDENTIFICATION CLAIM -- verified against the actual code, not taken on the document's word. Read apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts directly: `AgendaItem { kind: string; at: string; label: string }` (line 48) matches the document's citation exactly. `validateAgenda` (lines 68-89) genuinely uses `item.kind === "doors"` at both the multiple-doors count (line 73) and the doors-after-start check (line 80) -- the document's 'line 73/80' citation is accurate, not invented. `validateAgenda` also genuinely enforces at most one doors item (line 73-76, `doorsCount > 1` -> refuse), so 'the doors item' is well-defined for every event this design will ever read, exactly as claimed.

2. AC7 BYTE-IDENTITY CLAIM -- verified against REQ-017's actual renderer, not assumed. Read domain/event.ts's `buildEventCardContent` (lines 824-862): `agendaLines` maps every agenda item via `formatDateTimeInTimezone(new Date(item.at), event.chapterTimezone, lang)` (line 847). REQ-026's proposed T-3h doors line calls `formatDateTimeInTimezone(new Date(doorsItem.at), event.chapterTimezone, lang)` -- identical function, identical three arguments, identical order, identical `new Date(...)` wrapping. Structurally byte-identical as claimed; not a coincidence of two independently-written format calls.

3. AC8 NEGATIVE CASE -- correctly designed, not a loose match. Sec3.2's table states: agenda non-null with no element whose `kind === "doors"` -> `findDoorsAgendaItem` returns `null` (not 'first item', not any other loose heuristic). Sec5.2's closing paragraph additionally confirms the composition loop never iterates `agenda` for anything but this one lookup, so no other item's time (networking/close) can leak into the caption. Correct.

4. `reconfirmed_at` CLAIM -- verified true, not a MAJOR finding. `grep -rn "reconfirmed_at|reconfirmedAt" apps/bot/src apps/bot/drizzle` finds the column in apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts line 261 exactly as cited (`reconfirmedAt: timestamp("reconfirmed_at", { withTimezone: true })`), present since migration 0001, with zero writers anywhere in apps/bot/src today (only schema.ts/migration/snapshot hits) -- genuinely unused until this design's first writer. docs/agents/design/REQ-011.md line 218/406 confirms REQ-011 is the design of record that added it ('a pre-event reconfirmation nudge... nullable because most registrations are never reconfirmed or the feature hasn't fired yet'). Claim accurate; DATA-DESIGNER is correctly not required for this run.

5. NotificationSender EXTENSION vs. REQ-025's S9/S10 guarantees -- traced against the live apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts and scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, not assumed compatible. Today's `sendLedgeredNotification` steps 1-4 (user resolution, blocked check, marketing-only broadcastOptIn check, the atomic ledger INSERT that is S9's entire idempotency mechanism via UNIQUE(registration_id, kind)) are stated by the design as unchanged, and are genuinely unaffected by the proposed extension: only step 5 (composeMessage's return shape and the sender call it drives) changes. The ledger INSERT (step 4) still happens, unconditionally, before composeMessage is ever invoked (step 5) -- the insert-then-send ordering that is the substance of AC1/S9's crash-restart guarantee is untouched; a `skipped-stale` outcome from an at-send-time recheck happens strictly after the ledger row has already committed, matching REQ-025 Sec3.2's already-accepted 'once consumed, never reattempted' risk, not a new one. S10's classification gate (step 3, unconditional broadcastOptIn read only for `classification === "marketing"`) is untouched by the extension -- Sec1.2's rule table only modifies branching inside step 5, never step 3. `sendPhoto`'s design (Sec1.3) is stated to share the identical pacing/backoff rule table as `send` (same rolling window, same retry/backoff/exhaustion behavior) -- verified against the live rateLimiter.ts (RollingWindowPacer, sendWithRetry) that this is a faithful, unmodified reuse of the existing mechanism substituting only the underlying bot.api call, not a second independently-configured channel. No regression to either invariant.

6. index.ts SEQUENCING BUG -- verified real, and the fix verified correct. Read apps/bot/src/index.ts directly: line 76 constructs `notificationSender`, line 77 calls `startScheduledJobs([])` immediately after, and there is no `bot.init()` call anywhere in the file today -- `bot.start()` is the sole grammY lifecycle call, at line 170 (the file's last line). The claimed bug is real: as written today this is masked only because REQ-025 passes an empty job list; REQ-026 ships real jobs whose composeMessage (Sec5.2 step 5) needs `botUsername` for `renderCheckInQrPng`, which without `bot.init()` having resolved would be read from an unpopulated `bot.botInfo`. The proposed fix (call and await `bot.init()`, then read `bot.botInfo.username` once, then call `startScheduledJobs([...])` with both real jobs, `bot.start()` remaining the file's last call, in that order) is the correct minimal fix with no other side effect on any of the file's other command/callback registrations, all of which are order-independent of this change.

7. AC1-AC10 -> DESIGN ELEMENT MAP -- re-derived against issue #29's ten ACs, not trusted from Sec10's own table. All ten map to concrete, non-deferred design elements: AC1 (Sec3.1 window + Sec5.1 single composeMessage/single sendLedgeredNotification call), AC2 (Sec4's decideReconfirmOutcome/reconfirmRegistration touching only reconfirmed_at + Sec7.1/7.2 handlers), AC3 (unchanged REQ-025 ledger UNIQUE guard, Sec1.2), AC4 (Sec3.1's admission='admitted' selection filter), AC5 (Sec5.2 steps 2/4/5), AC6 (Sec5.2 step 4, both lines always composed when doorsItem present), AC7 (item 2 above), AC8 (item 3 above), AC9 (Sec0's header + Sec0's confirmation of no doors_at column anywhere), AC10 (Sec5 point 2's `classification: "transactional"` on both jobs). No AC left addressed only by TBD/deferral language.

Verdict: FAIL on check 2d alone (Sec5.1 point 4, Sec5.2 point 4). Rework CODE-DESIGNER: restate the two composeMessage content-assembly blocks as prose/table rules per this project's own REQ-017/REQ-025 precedent; no other change required to the document as far as this validation could determine.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md Sec5.1 point 4 (T-24h composeMessage) and Sec5.2 point 4 (T-3h composeMessage) contain literal executable TypeScript -- an array literal composed with a real `.join("\n")` call, and inline template-literal string interpolation for the doors/start caption lines and button callback_data -- rather than a prose or table statement of the composition rule. This fails WF-02 Step 1b check 2d (no implementation code) and is a direct instance of the exact anti-pattern .claude/agents/code-designer.md names as having already FAILed this gate twice before ('a real one-line predicate... because it's obvious anyway is implementation, full stop'). REQ-017.md Sec3.2 and REQ-025.md Sec4 both describe structurally identical content-composition rules (agendaLines/dateTimeText; composeMessage's text) entirely in prose/table form with no literal array/join/template-literal code, establishing the correct convention this document should have followed. Rework: rewrite both blocks as an ordered-lines prose table (what each line is, its source fields, the join character), keeping all content/field-sourcing decisions unchanged.
